# Flight computer verification report

*Generated by `scripts/verification_report.py` on 2026-10-03 20:15 from commit `757990f`. Do not edit by hand: re-run `scripts/run_sil_montecarlo.py` and this script.*

**Campaign:** 500 seeded SIL flights (seed 20261003), 207 nominal and 293 with one random fault. Every flight was flown by **both** detectors (Kalman = the default FC, and the raw-barometer baseline) on identical inputs. The dispersions are the same as `run_montecarlo.py`: wind speed and direction, motor impulse, Cd, dry mass and rail angle. Pad sits: 1000 × 60 s. Campaign time: 6.4 min on 8 workers.

Requirement texts and rationale: [requirements.md](requirements.md). Design reasoning: [fc_walkthrough.md](fc_walkthrough.md).

## 1. Requirement verdicts (default Kalman FC)

| Requirement | Evidence | Result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **REQ-001** Nominal flight: the FC deploys within 0.5 s of true apogee. | 207 Monte Carlo runs; 3 tagged tests | 207/207 pass (100.0 %); 3/3 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-002** Zero false launch detections across 1000 seeded 60 s pad sits. | 1000 pad sits × 60 s; 3 tagged tests | 0 false launches, 0 false sensor failures; 3/3 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-003** The FC never commands deployment while the rocket is on the pad or under thrust, under any fault. | 500 Monte Carlo runs; 21 tagged tests | 500/500 pass (100.0 %); 21/21 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-004** Under any single sensor or link fault, the FC deploys within 1.5 s of true apogee or via its backup timer; a run where the FC never deploys fails. | 257 Monte Carlo runs; 24 tagged tests | 257/257 pass (100.0 %); 24/24 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-005** An FC hang is detected by the watchdog and the parachute is still deployed (motor backup charge). | 36 Monte Carlo runs; 7 tagged tests | 36/36 pass (100.0 %); 7/7 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-006** FC output is deterministic: identical input gives identical output. | 10 worst-case replays; 6 tagged tests | 10/10 bit-identical; 6/6 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-007** A malformed, garbled or stale FC reply never causes a deployment. | 15 tagged tests | 15/15 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-008** The FC answers every input line with exactly one line and survives malformed input. | 2 tagged tests | 2/2 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-009** On a nominal flight the FC deploys from apogee detection, never from its backup timer. | 207 Monte Carlo runs; 3 tagged tests | 207/207 pass (100.0 %); 3/3 tests pass | ✅ PASS |
| **REQ-010** On a nominal flight the FC reports LANDED within 10 s of touchdown. | 207 Monte Carlo runs; 3 tagged tests | 207/207 pass (100.0 %); 3/3 tests pass | ✅ PASS |

**Overall: all requirements verified.**

## 2. Baseline vs Kalman (identical inputs)

Deploy error = FC deploy command time − true apogee time. |dt| p95 is the 95th percentile of |error| over runs where that FC commanded deployment. "Req" is the class's governing requirement (REQ-001 for nominal runs, REQ-005 for hangs, REQ-004 otherwise).

| Fault class | Runs | Kalman mean | Kalman \|dt\| p95 | Kalman timer | Kalman req | Baseline mean | Baseline \|dt\| p95 | Baseline req |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Nominal (no fault) | 207 | +0.044 s | 0.057 s | 0 | 207/207 | +0.520 s | 0.639 s | 70/207 |
| Link blackout | 32 | +0.217 s | 1.016 s | 2 | 32/32 | +0.570 s | 0.828 s | 32/32 |
| Random frame loss | 41 | +0.067 s | 0.131 s | 0 | 41/41 | +0.583 s | 0.707 s | 41/41 |
| Stuck barometer | 27 | +0.039 s | 0.064 s | 0 | 27/27 | +1.088 s | 1.293 s | 27/27 |
| Stuck accelerometer | 33 | +0.502 s | 0.617 s | 0 | 33/33 | +0.512 s | 0.617 s | 33/33 |
| Barometer spikes | 30 | +0.083 s | 0.055 s | 1 | 30/30 | -4.260 s | 4.865 s | 0/30 |
| Accelerometer spikes | 27 | +0.215 s | 1.247 s | 4 | 27/27 | +0.505 s | 0.615 s | 27/27 |
| Barometer drift | 35 | +0.074 s | 0.336 s | 0 | 35/35 | +0.566 s | 0.875 s | 35/35 |
| Accelerometer drift | 32 | +0.577 s | 1.236 s | 16 | 32/32 | +0.516 s | 0.600 s | 32/32 |
| FC hang | 36 | +0.046 s | 0.049 s | 0 | 36/36 | +0.516 s | 0.608 s | 36/36 |

Per-run requirement pass rates for the **baseline** FC (for comparison only; requirements apply to the default FC): REQ-001 70/207, REQ-003 500/500, REQ-004 227/257, REQ-005 36/36, REQ-009 207/207, REQ-010 207/207.

**Reading it:**
* On nominal flights, the Kalman FC deploys about 0.05 s after apogee. The baseline deploys about 0.5 s after, and misses REQ-001's 0.5 s window on most flights.
* Under faults the gap widens. The baseline has no outlier defence (one barometer spike inflates its running maximum and it deploys seconds early) and no stuck-sensor isolation.
* "Kalman timer" counts runs where the FC detected a fault it couldn't isolate and deployed by its backup timer. That's the designed safe outcome (walkthrough §8.4).

## 3. Which mechanism deployed the chute (Kalman FC)

| Mechanism | Runs |
|---|---:|
| fc (apogee) | 448 |
| motor | 29 |
| fc (backup_timer) | 23 |

The motor charge (C6-7, about 1.4 s after apogee) deploys first only when the FC hung before apogee (REQ-005), or in the rare case where the FC's own backup timer fires later than the charge.

## 6. Harness notes

* The watchdog uses wall-clock time, the only wall-clock element in the loop. A first campaign with a 1.0 s timeout falsely declared one healthy FC failed under heavy host load: a replay of the run was clean. The timeout is now 3 s, and any watchdog trip on a run *without* an injected hang is re-run once. The FC is deterministic, so a genuine hang reproduces and a host artefact doesn't.
* Unexpected watchdog trips in this campaign: **0** (reproduced on re-run: 0).

## 7. Limits of this verification

* It is SIL, not HIL. Lockstep doesn't exercise real-time deadlines or the CPU budget.
* Sensor models and fault magnitudes are engineering assumptions (see `sim/sensors.py` and `sim/faults.py`). They are not measured hardware data.
* Single faults only. Double faults are outside the requirements (walkthrough §8.8).
* Pass rates are for this campaign's sample size. Zero failures in N runs bounds the per-run failure probability below about 3/N at 95 % confidence (the "rule of three"): for N = 500, below 0.6%.
